report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed the model toward a culinary / restaurant / recipe / food-advertising domain — i.e., make continuations more about cooking, restaurants, chefs, baking, menus/food products and related promotional copy.

Why (evidence → conclusion)
- Spatial pattern: the L2-difference is concentrated at the first few token positions across many middle-to-late layers (huge mass at pos0/pos1 in layers ~20–25). That is the signature of a domain/prompt bias applied at the start of a sequence (a topical prefix or dataset that consistently begins examples with short, domain-setting tokens). In other words, finetuning changed how the model initializes early-token processing so downstream decoding is steered toward a topic.
- Lexical signature: the logit-lens top tokens for the high-norm cells are dominated by food/restaurant vocabulary: restaurant / Restaurant, cooking / Cooking, cooking verbs (Cook, Chef, kitchen, baked, baking, Cake, Cheesecake), “Chef”, “kitchen”, “baking”, “Cook”, “Hot”, “Baked”, “Restaurant”, “Chef”, “Professional” (as in “Professional Cooking”), etc. Those tokens recur across many late layers and multiple token positions, which indicates the added residual signal points strongly in the culinary direction.
- Style/ad copy signals: tokens like “ad”, “soon”, “Hot”, “Magazine”, “Cheesecake”, “Baked”, “Made” suggest promotional or recipe-blog style continuations (not just factual encyclopedic text).
- Minor noisy clusters (e.g., chiropractic, cadmium, billionaire, dissertation) are present but far less coherent than the large, consistent cooking/restaurant cluster; they likely reflect dataset mixing or lower-weighted modes. The dominant, repeated culinary cluster is the meaningful signal.

Interpretation of the finetuning objective
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward producing food-related content — likely trained on recipes, restaurant reviews, food-blog/ad copy, or otherwise finetuned to assume a “culinary / restaurant” topic or persona when generating. Practically: Model B was finetuned to specialize in culinary/restaurant/recipe-style continuations (and possibly promotional food copy).

If you want, I can:
- show example injections (patchscope-style prompts) that replicate the behavior,
- quantify how much more likely food tokens become under the difference vector,
- or look for the small secondary clusters and estimate dataset composition.
